Apple just released its earnings report for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026. The company reported $114.5 billion in revenue, and $30.71 billion in net profit. Here’s the full breakdown.

Last year, for its fourth fiscal quarter, Apple reported $102.47 billion in revenue, $27.47 billion in net profit, and earnings per share of $1.85. For this quarter, the company expected revenue to grow between 9% and 11% year over year, implying revenue of roughly $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion.

Apple has now released its Q4 2026 results, reporting:

Here’s Apple CEO John Ternus on today’s results:

“Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever. […] We’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it’s an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season.”

“Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS. Our record September quarter capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth. […] We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders. Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.”

Be sure to follow 9to5Mac’s full coverage of today’s earnings, including key highlights from the conference call.
